Akaḍamacakra
yoga-tantra. Akaḍama is a Tāntrik diagram described in the Rudrayāmala (Vācaspatya). See also MD. 7847, Tantrasāra, list of contents, where Akaḍamacakra is mentioned.
Dacca 298-I. IM. 11182. JBhP. I. 1. Jodhpur 853. IO. Keith, p. 681a, last line, shows that IO. 6093 deals with Akaḍamacakra an. other Cakras.

Akaḍamacakracitra
similar to the above. B. IV. 252.

Akaḍaha-ṛṇadhanacaka
similar to the above. Ujjain I. p. 73. [Page002-b]

Akathahacakra
similar to the above. Allahabad 139. AS. p. 1. Bharatpur I. 385. See also MD. 14714 an. 7847, Tantrasāra, list of contents, for this Cakra.

Akabaranāma
or sarvadezavRttAntasaGgraha by Maheśa Ṭhakkura, the logician; a Skt. transl. of the Akbarnāmah in Persian, on the life of Akbar.
C.. VI. 5. IO. 4106. Sūcīpattra 126. For a note on the latter ms., see Allahabad University Studies I, p.. 15-17.

Akabaraśāhīśṛṅgāradarpaṇa
kāvya. by Padmasundara. Bikaner 9356.
Pt.. Gaṅgā. Ori. Ser. 1, Bikaner, 1943.

Akabaraṣā(baḍe_Sāheb),
of the family of Gesu Daraj of Gulbarga; son of Shah Raju, teacher of Abul Hasan, Qutb Shah of Golconda (died 1704 A. D.).
--Śṛṅgāramañjarī. Mysore II. p. 14. TD. 11001.
Ed.. V. Raghavan, Hyderabad Arch. Dept., 1951.

Akabarīyakālidāsa
poet of the court of Akbar, cited in later anthologies. IO. Keith, p. 1157b. Cal. Ori. Jour. III. 5. p.. 136-7.
Real name Govindabhaṭṭa. See IHQ. XVII. p.. 257-8; also Bikaner, p. 230.
--Birudāvalī. Rep. Raj. & C. I. p. 39.
--Rāmacandrayaśah2prabandha, praise of King Rāmacandra of Rewa, a contemporary of Akbar.
Bik. 522 (Auf. C.. I p. 167b). Bikaner 3080. RASB. IV. 3109.

Akartṛtvabhoktṛtvaprakaraṇa
with metrical Hindi C. Skt. Col.. Ben. 1897-1901. p. 240 (no. 1002) (inc.). [Page003-a.

Akarmakādiprayoga
gr. tract on voices of verbal forms for beginners. Adyar II. p. 88a.

Akalaṅka
Dig. Jain logician. Wilson, Mack. Cat. p. lxi. Sewell, Antiq. of Madras, p. 265. Epi. Car. II. Insc. 64 (A. D. 1163) gives the teachers up to Akalaṅka. Insc. 67 mentions Ak.'s dispute with the Buddhists a. Kāñcī. Also ibid. Intro. p.. 48, 68, 84, 85; Vol. VI. Intro. p. 30. Mys. Arch. Rep. 1917. p. 24. Rice, Mysore II. p. 366. JRAS. NS. XV. p. 299. Epi. Ind. IV. 22 ff. JBBRAS. XVIII. p. 223. ABORI. XI. p. 155; XIII. p.. 157-160. p.. 161 ff. Peters. V. Index of authors, p. i. R. G. B. Rep. 1883-4. p. 122. S. C. Vidyabhushana, HIL. p.. 185-6. W. Schubring, Die Lehre der Jainas, p.. 39, 44, 46. ZDMG. 68, p. 695.
Said to have been a contemporary of the Rāṣṭrakūṭa Śubhatuṅga or Kṛṣṇa I, first half of the 8th cent.; was a priest a. Śravaṇabelgola; defeated the Bauddhas a. the court of a Pallava King of Kāñcī named He(Hi)maśītala an. drove the Bauddhas to Kandy in Ceylon. See MD. XI. p. 3977. Epi. Car. II. Insc. 67. “In the 8th cent. again, Akalaṅka went from Śravaṇabelgola in Mysore to the Buddhist College a. Ponataga in the North Arcot D.. for study.” Epi. Car. VI. Intro. p. 30. On Hemaśītala's probable identity with Hiraṇyavarman, father of Nandivarman Pallavamalla, see Journal Mad. Uni. I. ii. Sup. p. 41. The Kanarese work Himaśītalakathe gives his story. Mys. Arch. Rep. 1918. p. 68: in a Skt. work called Bhuvanapradīpikā written in 1808, Himaśītala is mentioned among Jain [Page003-b] kings of Kāñcī a. having ruled from Kali 1125 an. in his reign Ak. is said to have confuted the Bauddhas.
Rice, Intro. to his Ed.. of the Karṇātakaśabdānuśāsana, p.. 24-5, says that according to Jain tradition, Akalaṅka defeated the Bauddhas a. Kāñcī in A. D. 855.
Epi. Car. II. p. 84: “Akalaṅkacarita, a small Skt. work, gives Vik. 700 a. the year in which Ak. defeated the Bauddhas a. Kāñcī.” On Akalaṅka traditions a. Tiruppanamūr, 12 miles from Kāñcī, see Madras Museum Bulletin, III, Tirupparuttikunram an. its Temples, 1937, p. 42.
Peterson, II, p. 79: according to a.Dig. Kathākośa, Akalaṅka an. Niṣkalaṅka were the two sons of King Śubhatuṅga of Mānyakheṭa, i. e. Kṛṣṇarāja, the Rāṣṭrakūṭa King, 753-755 A. D. Akalaṅka then became a monk. See also Yaśastilakacampūvyākhyā, p. 236. K. M. 70, part I.
In Akalaṅka's Tattvārthabhāṣya we find a verse calling him son of a King, Laghu Habva (laghuhabvanRpativaratanayaH).
According to Nemidatta's Ārādhanākathākośa, Akalaṅka was the son of Puruṣottama, a. Brahmin minister of King Śubhatuṅga of Mānyakheṭa.
The Kanarese work Rājāvalikathe, 8th section, gives the story of Akalaṅka an. Himaśītala. Here father given a. a. Arhaddvija an. brother Niṣkalaṅka; studied under a Bauddha named Bhagavaddāsa; fought the Śaivas a. Sudhāpura.
In some edns. of the Akalaṅkastotra, a Jinadāsa is given a. Ak.'s father Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1906-28. 31-32. [Page004-a.
Wint. HIL. II. p. 478. fn. 4: “Ak. lived during the reign of the Rāṣṭrakūṭa king Sāhasatuṅga Dantidurga.”
Insc. 54 a. Śravaṇabelgola refers to Ak. an. Sāhasatuṅga.
See also Mys. Arch. Rep. 1925, p. 13: Ak. latter part of the 8th cent. an. partly in the beginning of the 9th.; also Epoch of Kūṇa Pāṇḍya, AIOC. Proceed. III, p.. 225-6.
See ABORI. XII. p. 255, for A. D. 645 a. Ak.'s date.
ABORI. XI. p. 155: mid. 8th cent.; also in ABORI. XIII. p.. 157-160, where he is held a. a. elder contemporary of his commentator, Prabhācandra.
ABORI. XIII. p. 165 fn.: Ak.'s date in the last quarter of the 7th cent. a. the latest. The Akalaṅkacarita assigns A. D. 643 to Ak. Also Upadhye's Intro. to his edn. of the Pravacanasāra, p.. lxxx fn., cl. fn. 2.
See also the Jaina Hitaiṣī, XI. 7-8; Jain Anti. III. iv. p.. 149-165; IV. iii. p.. 165-175. See also Intro.. to the Nyāyakumudacandra, Bombay, an. Akalaṅkagranthatraya, Singhī Jain Ser. 12, 1939. In the last, Ak. is assigned to the 8th. cent.
See also Jour. Bombay His.. Soc. VI, i-ii, 1941, p.. 10-33.
--Akalaṅkasūtra (with Anantavīrya's gloss) mentioned in Insc. 35 of Nagar, Mysore; Mysore an. Coorg, p. 199. ABORI. XIII. p.. 161-170, says that this Ak. sūtra on which a. Anantavīrya is said to have written a C. may refer to the Kārikās of Siddhiviniścaya of Ak. or to the Pramāṇasaṅgrahasūtras of Ak. [Page004-b]
--Akalaṅkastotra or Akalaṅkāṣṭaka.
--Aṣṭaśatī, C. on Samantabhadra's Āptamīmāṁsā.
--Tattvārthavārttikālaṅkāra or Rājavārttikālaṅkāra, C. on the Tattvārthādhigamasūtras of Umāsvāti.
BORI. 1070 of 1891-95, Tattvakaustubha by Akalaṅka, is only ch. 7 of this same work.
Ed. Sanātana Jaina Granthamālā 4, Banaras 1915.
--Devāgamastotranyāsa. Mentioned also in Insc. 105 of Śravaṇabelgola (Rice, Mysore an. Coorg, p. 200).
--Nyāyacūlikā. Jain Anti. III. iv. p. 160.
--Nyāyaviniścaya. Pannalal Bombay, 113 (N. v. alaṅkāra by Ak.). Strassburg Dig. p. 9. Pathak (ABORI. XII, p. 373) an. S. C. Vidyabhushana (HIL p. 198) mention a gloss on this by a. Anantavīrya. Upadhye (ABORI. XIII. p.. 161-170) doubts this, since no ms. of this C. has come to light.
A ms. of Nyāyaviniścaya with Vādirāja's gloss is preserved in the Arrah Library. Arrah, p. 45. See also Jain Anti. III. iv. p. 160. Restored from Vādirāja's gloss an. ed. in the Akalaṅkagranthatraya, Singhī Jain Ser. 12, 1939.
--Pramāṇaratnapradīpa. JRAS. XV. p. 299.
--Pramāṇalakṣaṇa, Mysore I. p. 557.
--Pramāṇasaṅgraha (8 sections). Jaina Sid. Bhās. III. i. p.. 1-6, Extracts. Anantavīrya has written a C. on this work. Ed. in Akalaṅkagranthatraya, Singhī Jain Ser. 12 (9 sections). [Page005-a.
--Prāyaścitta or Prā. grantha or Prā. vidhi or Śrāvakavidhi. Authorship doubted by some.
BORI. 1086 of 1884-87. 1110 of 1891-95. Wint. HIL. II. p. 581. Hiralal, CPB. Intro., p.. xxvi.
Ed. in Māṇik. Dig. Jain Granth. 18.
--Bṛhattrayī. Jain Grantha Bhandar, Kolhapur. Jain Anti. III. iv. p. 160.
--Laghīyastraya with his own C. Ed. in the Akalaṅkagranthatraya, Singhī Jain Ser. 12; also in Māṇik. Dig. Jain Granth. 1.
On Laghīyastraya, Prabhācandra wrote a gloss called Nyāyakumudacandra or Ny. ku. ca. udaya, from which it appears, that in some mss. the name Nyāyakumudacandra has been wrongly given to the Laghīyastraya itself. See Jainagranthāvalī, p. 91, a. also edn. of Laghīyastraya in Akalaṅkagranthatraya, Singhī Jain Ser. cols. up to p. 15 an. fn. p. 3.
--Vādasindhu ? Intro. to the Pāṇḍavapurāṇa. See MT. 1388. Is ‘Vādasindhu’ a logic treatise of Ak. or is it a mere figurative description of Ak.'s works in general ? It is reported that there is a work called Akalaṅkavāda in the Jain monastery a. Śittambūr, Tindivanam Tq., S. I.
--Siddhiviniścaya. in Vādideva's Syādvādaratnākara, Ārhatamataprabhākara edn. p. 641. Anantavīrya has written a C. on this. A ms. of this is said to be available in the Gujarat Vidyāpīṭh, Ahmedabad; (ABORI. XIII, p.. 161-170), but a catalogue of this collection supplied to the NCC. does not mention that ms. [Page005-b]
--Svarūpasambodhana or Sv.. sam. pañcaviṁśati.
Ed. Māṇik. Dig. Jain Granth. 1.

Akalaṅka
Jain.
--Paramāgamasāra. Arrah I. p. 18.

Akalaṅka
Jain.
--Vivekamañjarīvṛtti. Jainagranthāvalī p. 188. Since Āsaḍa wrote his Vivekamañjarī in A. D. 1192, this Ak. must be later than an. different from the celebrated logician (Aṣṭaśatī etc.) noticed above.

Akalaṅkakavi
--Vrataphalavarṇanā. Pt.. with Kanarese gloss, along with Akalaṅkāṣṭaka, Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1892-1906. 23. [Page006-a.

Akalaṅkacarita
on the life of Ak. (Aṣṭaśatī etc.). Mysore I. p. 552. Śravaṇabelgola 384. On the date it gives to Ak., see ABORI. XIII. p. 165 fn. an. Epi. Car. II. p. 84. Mys. Arch. Rep. 1917, p. 24.

Akalaṅkadeva
Jain.
--Caityavandanādisūtra-sādhuśrāddhapratikramaṇapadaparyāyamañjarī.
Jainagranthāvalī p.. 28. 58. This apparently single entry contains evidently the titles of a. least two works.
C.. BORI. List p. 31 (845 of 1895-1902) -- Śrāvakapratikramaṇapadaparyāyamañjarī.

Akalaṅkadeva
Jain.
--Citrakāvya. (probably Saṁ. 1574). See Anekānt I. 373-75.

Akalaṅkadeva
Jain.
--Nyāyakumudacandra. Jainagranthāvalī p. 91. Is this a wrong entry for Prabhācandra's Nyāyakumudacandrodaya on Ak.'s Laghīyastraya ?

Akalaṅkapratiṣṭhākalpa
(-pATha or -vidhi) See Akalaṅkasaṁhitā below.

Akalaṅkasaṃhitā
or aka. pratiSThAkalpa or aka. pra. pATha or aka. pra. vidhi. Jain. consecration by Bhaṭṭa Akalaṅkadeva; follows Nemicandra.
Arrah II. 48. Mysore I. p.. 360. 552. Pannalal Bombay IV. p. 1. Śravaṇabelgola 195.
For Extr., see Jaina Sid. Bhās. VII. 1. Praśasti, p.. 165-8.

Akalaṅkasūtra
Jain logic. by Akalaṅka.
--C. by Anantavīrya.
Insc. 35 Nagar, Mysore. Mysore an. Coorg, Insc. from, p. 199. In ABORI. XIII. p.. 161-170, it is suggested that this Ak. sūtra is either Ak.'s [Page006-b] kārikās in his Siddhiviniścaya or Ak.'s Pramāṇasaṅgrahasūtras. S. C. Vidyabhushana, HIL. p. 198, mentions Anantavīrya a. having commented on Ak.'s Nyāyaviniścaya which is doubted by some (ABORI. XIII. p.. 161-170).

Akalaṅkastotra
or akalaGkASTaka Jain. stotra. The information in MD. 9424 that this is a stotra in praise of Akalaṅka himself, the logician, an. that in IO. 7600 that it is on Śiva are both wrong. The Stotra is on Arhan who is said to be the real Śiva (Maṅgala), the real Viṣṇu (Vyāpaka) an. so on. Keith's surmise under IO. 7600 that, in MD. 9424, there are a Śivastotra an. a. Akalaṅkastotra, is also wrong.
Adyar II. p. 240b (2 mss.). AK. 1044. Arrah I. p. 1 (9 mss.). BORI. 1393 of 1886-92. 1044 of 1891-95. 94G of 1898-99 (last with Ṭippaṇa). BORI. D. XIX. 575-7 (last with C.). CPB. 6922-3. 6924 (?) (gives 6924 a. a different stotra in 9 verses an. mentions the former, 6922-3, a. a stotra in 16 verses; calls the latter Aṣṭaka, the former simply stotra. MD. 9424 has 16 verses in all). Delhi II. 100k. Hombucca 149. IO. 7600. Jhalrapatan p.. 33. 77 (a..). 81. Lakṣmīsena p.. 19. 31. 39. MD. 9424 (with 3 verses on the author a. the end referring to his defeating the Buddhists in the court of Himaśītala a. Kāñcī). 15611 (with Kanarese meaning). Moodbidri I. 121. 227k. II. 185b. 272c. 284e. 380c. 390d. 679b. Mysore I. p. 552. Pannalal Bombay. I. p. 50 (2 mss.). V. B. p. 6. Peters. IV. 52. VI. p. 143. PUL. II. p. 290. Strassburg Dig. p. 2. [Page007-a.

Akalaṅkasvāmin
Jain.

Akalaṅkācārya

Akalaṅkāṣṭaka

Akahacakra

Akārādiśabdamañjarī

Akārādisahasranāmāvali

Akālakavyākaraṇa
a name of Pāṇini's Gr. a. it is devoid of Kālaparibhāṣā. See Kāśikā on Pāṇini II. 4. 21, Haradatta on I. 2. 57, Jinendrabuddhi an. Mādhavīyadhātuvṛtti an. Kielhorn. Ind. Ant. XV. 1886. p. 184b ff.

Akālaghana
title of Cāmuṇḍasiṁha, a king on the banks of the Sarayū; of the Mohammedan period; name of a C. on the Vyaktiviveka of Mahimabhaṭṭa caused to be written by this king. Rep. Raj. & C. I. p.. 39-40 an. 85-87.

Akālacandra
jy. Ani (2 mss.).

Akālajalada
poet; great-grandfather of Rājaśekhara. Bālarāmāyaṇa, Prastāvanā, śl. 13. Described here a. a.‘Mahārāṣṭracūḍāmaṇi.’ See also Peterson's Intro. to Sbhv. p. 102.
Śp. 777 an. Sbhv. 843: the same verse given over the names ‘Akālajalada’ an. ‘Dākṣiṇātya’, from which [Page008-a. Akālajalada appears to have been a southerner.
‘Akālajalada’ is not the real name of the poet; it was given to him for the expression ‘Akālajalada’ in the third line of the verse Śp. 777. Sbhv. 843:
tasmin zuSkasarasyakAlajaladenAgatya tacceSTitam |
According to a eulogistic verse on Akālajalada by Rājaśekhara found in the Sūktimuktāvalī of Jalhaṇa, a poet named Kādambarīrāma used Akālajalada's verses in his drama an. became famous a. a dramatist:
akAlajaladazlokaizcitramAtmakRtairiva | jAtaH kAdambarIrAmo nATake pravaraH kaviH ||
Akālajalada an. his description of the rains are introduced by Somadeva in his Yaśastilakacampū, K. M. 70., part 1, p.. 543-48.

Akāladantakalpa
Jain. Jainagranthāvalī p. 364.

Akālaprasavaśānti
dh. MT. 437 (fol. 19b).

Akālabhāskara
